To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the generalized Poisson process is a good model for the number or defaults of a pool, that a tractable and flexible model for the pool loss can be obtained using the generalized Poisson loss model, that the generalized Poison model is a tractable and accurate model for CDO tranche pricing, and that the generalized Poissons model can be used to calibrate CDO tranches to quoted prices.

the generalized Poisson model for the number-of-defaults is a tractable and flexible approach for pricing and calibrating index CDOs and tranchelets, and that the pool-loss model, although less flexible, provides a good alternative.
the generalized-Poisson and piecewise-gamma models provide a good calibration fit to the market, and that the CIR model is more flexible and stable than the gamma model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the calibration of the CDO market to a dynamical loss process, with the aim of obtaining tractable and realistic models.
the modeling of CDO tranches with the aim of providing a consistent calibration to the quoted market.
the modeling and calibration of credit derivatives, and more specifically of CDOs and CDO tranches.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the generalized-Poisson loss model is a flexible and tractable model for the pricing of credit indices, and that the CIR extension is a promising approach to model the spread dynamics.
the generalized-Poisson model is a good model to price CDO tranches, but that the CIR model is a good alternative to price tranchelets.
the generalized-Poisson approach is a very promising candidate for the modeling of CDO tranches.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a tractable model that can be calibrated to quoted index tranche prices and tranchelet prices, with a good fit to the market.
the generalized-Poisson model provides a simple, yet tractable, framework for modeling the pool loss, which is flexible enough for consistent calibration to CDO tranches.
the generalized Poisson process is a very useful tool for modeling the number of defaults, and the pool loss, in CDOs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple model can be used to price CDO tranches with a good level of accuracy, even when the underlying pool of reference is not homogeneous.

, in the context of CDO tranches, the dynamical generalized-Poisson model can be calibrated to a large number of tranches and maturities, and that the calibration is stable, even with a small number of parameters, contrary to other approaches.
a tractable and flexible model can be obtained by combining a dynamical generalized-Poisson process with a piecewise-gamma intensity.
